title: Ledger and Clock
premise: In 1899, Edmund Ashgrove, a quiet apprentice clockmaker, is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock just as the army requisitions the town and its ledger of names for evacuation berths. Hidden within the clock's case, Edmund discovers his late mother's letters revealing he was smuggled out of a debtors' colony as a child—meaning the Ashgroves who raised him are not blood kin at all. As the deadline approaches and only one berth remains in the found family that claimed him, Edmund must decide whether to surrender it to save himself or forge the ledger one last time. He gives up his own name, stays behind with the clock, and rings in 1900 as the town's new keeper of time—and keeper of everyone's names.
about_author: Elodie Yarrow is the pen name of a former horologist's assistant who spent a decade restoring Victorian tower clocks across northern England before turning to fiction. Her novels blend meticulous period craft with intimate stories of people history forgot to record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He arrives at the observatory town of Hallowmere, keeping his head down among the master clockmaker's household—the warm, chaotic Ashgrove family who took him in years ago. He begins diagnosing the master clock's failure. Emotional beat: cautious belonging, the comfort of being useful rather than known.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Everyone
chapters.summary: Marigold Ashgrove's POV. The town clerk shows Marigold the great ledger recording every resident's name, birth, and trade—a civic ritual Edmund has always avoided signing. She notices her son's absence from its pages. Emotional beat: maternal unease beneath domestic warmth.

chapters.title: Drums on the Ridge Road
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Army scouts arrive; an officer announces the valley will be requisitioned as a winter garrison and all residents registered by ledger for transport. The observatory becomes a requisition office. Emotional beat: dread arriving in polished boots.

chapters.title: What the Clock Keeps
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Repairing the master clock's chime mechanism, Edmund pries loose a hidden panel and finds bundled letters in his mother's hand—letters naming a debtors' colony and a child given away. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past ticking louder than the present.

chapters.title: Names, Taken Down
chapters.summary: Sergeant Corliss's POV. The registration begins; Corliss, weary and fair-minded, cross-examines residents against the ledger and flags discrepancies—including the Ashgrove household's unexplained apprentice. Emotional beat: bureaucratic menace with a flicker of conscience.

chapters.title: Berths and Bargains
chapters.summary: Marigold's POV. The family learns only a handful of civilian berths remain on the last transport before the garrison seals the valley. Old Tom Ashgrove quietly offers his place to Edmund. Emotional beat: love expressed as arithmetic.

chapters.title: Letters Not Meant for Me
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Reading the letters by candlelight, Edmund learns his mother died in the colony and that 'Ashgrove' was the name of the family who never asked questions. He lies at breakfast about the clock's progress. Emotional beat: grief braided with guilt over deceiving the people who saved him.

chapters.title: The Officer's Own Ledger
chapters.summary: Captain Vane's POV. Vane arrives to audit the requisition, suspicious of sentimentality in his subordinates and irregularities in the rolls. He orders the master clock seized as army property—its brass worth more than its timekeeping. Emotional beat: cold ambition meeting living tradition.

chapters.title: Apprentice of No Record
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Interrogated about his missing ledger entry, Edmund half-confesses his origins; Corliss, moved, warns him that Vane intends to strike undocumented persons from the transport list entirely. Emotional beat: exposure as both danger and strange relief.

chapters.title: Sisters of the Bell Rope
chapters.summary: Ivy Ashgrove's POV. Edmund's found-sister Ivy organizes the townsfolk to hide the colony-born families in the observatory cellars, treating strangers as kin without hesitation. Edmund watches her spend herself recklessly for others. Emotional beat: found family as active verb, not accident.

chapters.title: One Berth, Five Names
chapters.summary: Family council scene, rotating close-third between Edmund, Marigold, and Tom. With one berth left, each argues someone else should take it—Tom, then Marigold, then Edmund himself. Emotional beat: fierce tenderness weaponized into self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: Forging Midnight
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund secretly practices forging ledger entries, using his engraver's skill to alter names—an act that feels like betrayal of every honest hour he's ever worked. Emotional beat: the craftsman's conscience cracking under love.

chapters.title: Vane Inspects the Works
chapters.summary: Captain Vane's POV. Vane tours the clocktower, admiring the mechanism while planning to melt it for munitions fittings. He catches Edmund mid-repair and, probing him about the hidden panel, reveals he knows documents were concealed there. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse inside the gear train.

chapters.title: The Night the Chime Failed
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Sabotaged by a requisition clerk, the master clock stops dead at midnight before the whole garrison—a public humiliation Vane blames on Edmund. Arrest looms. Emotional beat: shame, then cold clarity about who his enemies are.

chapters.title: Corliss's Quiet Choice
chapters.summary: Sergeant Corliss's POV. Ordered to escort Edmund to detention, Corliss instead delays the paperwork, confessing he once lost his own family to a ledger like this one. He hands Edmund the audit schedule. Emotional beat: complicity turning to resistance.

chapters.title: All the Names at Once
chapters.summary: Edmund and Ivy's alternating POV. Working through the night, they rewrite the ledger—entering every hidden colonist under legitimate trades, distributing the single remaining berth across forged kinships so no one travels alone. Emotional beat: forgery transfigured into grace.

chapters.title: The Reckoning Hour
chapters.summary: Climax, Edmund's POV. Vane discovers the altered ledger during final inspection and confronts Edmund in the clockroom as the repaired mechanism nears completion. Edmund trades the truth—his mother's letters proving the colony's records were falsified first—for the family's passage. Emotional beat: truth as the only currency left.

chapters.title: Hands That Do Not Tremble
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund completes the escapement repair under Vane's eye, betting his life that the clock will run true. At noon it strikes perfectly, and even Vane cannot deny the workmanship—or publicly admit the fraud he now shares. Emotional beat: craft as courage; stillness inside terror.

chapters.title: Last Transport Before the Century
chapters.summary: Marigold's POV. On the frozen platform, the family boards—but Edmund's berth was quietly reassigned to old Tom, and Edmund remains behind, listed now as the clock's official keeper under Corliss's forged authorization. Emotional beat: farewell as inheritance passed forward.

chapters.title: Keeper of Hours
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Alone in the tower, Edmund winds the great clock, tends the cellar families awaiting spring papers, and writes his mother's name into the ledger at last. Emotional beat: solitude chosen, not imposed; grief settling into purpose.

chapters.title: Midnight, Nineteen Hundred
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, shifting briefly through Ivy's, Corliss's, and Edmund's eyes. The century turns; the master clock tolls twelve over a garrison town where every hidden name is finally spoken aloud at the New Year feast in the cellars. Emotional beat: collective exhale; time redeemed.

chapters.title: The First Entry of the New Century
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Edmund's POV. Spring brings amnesty papers and letters from the Ashgroves; Ivy returns to stand beside him as co-keeper. Edmund opens a fresh ledger page and writes the first new name—not his own, but a stranger's child newly arrived. Emotional beat: inheritance renewed; the clock, and the family, still running.
